This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 665059b6056c4caf54e631d678203d8c9dc4aba3` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2177e83aa4d555a287a78a78696c8b9717198e8c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-http-discovery-faults.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.test.ts + docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md (the upstream-availability, stdio-policy and scope-boundary sections), docs/adr/0024-mcp-connectors.md (sections 2 and 3), docs/adr/0023-openapi-to-connector-generator.md, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (the materializer's catch and the degraded-retry backoff), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/index.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/package.json, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/index.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/connector-openapi-plugin.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/system/connectors/status-openapi.json, pnpm-lock.yaml (the MCP SDK pin) and the pinned SDK's client/streamableHttp.js, client/auth.js, client/index.js and shared/protocol.js. The two changesets and content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx were read for section ②, not reviewed.

Inputs: card #26709 (body and all four comments, the os-dev-report included); PR #26798 (body, nine-file list, the net diff against main from the merge base a485b5a3); the check-runs on this head. Every required context is `success` — Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard; Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI and Build & E2E UI skipped on the path filter — and so are Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate and Spec property liveness; the two opt-in harnesses skipped. Since the base, main moved on packages/services/service-automation by one unrelated flow-screen commit and not on either connector package, the three ADRs or the docs page.

### ① Derived judgments

1. openapi provider — the document accept-set narrows at load: RIGHT. `loadOpenApiDocument` routes all three `providerConfig.spec` forms (inline object; http(s) URL after a 2xx and a successful parse; package file after a successful read and parse) through `assertOpenApi3Document`, which passes only a string `openapi` matching `3.N` or `3.N.M`. A `swagger: "2.0"` document, a document with no `openapi` field and `openapi: "4.0.0"` each throw a plain Error — never `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError` — so the materializer's existing split makes them fatal at boot and a logged, skipped entry on reload. The fault order is unchanged: an unreachable URL and 408/429/5xx still degrade; a non-retryable 4xx and an unparseable body still throw plain before the version check runs.
2. mcp provider — the materialization accept-set narrows on a rejected credential: RIGHT. In the catch around `createMcpConnector`, an error whose cause chain (walked eight deep) holds a `StreamableHTTPError` with `code` 401 or 403, or an `UnauthorizedError`, is rethrown plain with the status; everything else keeps `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError`, and a JSON-RPC `McpError` carrying 401 is not matched (pinned as a control). Verified against the pinned SDK (pnpm-lock: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1`): with no auth provider — this provider never wires one — `send()` throws `StreamableHTTPError(response.status, …)` for every non-ok POST, 401 and 403 included; `Protocol.request` rejects with that error unwrapped; `Client.connect` rethrows it after closing. So a 401 on the `initialize` POST, on the handshake or on `tools/list` reaches this catch as exactly the class tested for. `UnauthorizedError` is thrown only when an auth provider is wired, so that limb is unreachable on the default client today and correct for a future one.
3. mcp default client — `listTools` returns every page: RIGHT. Page 0 sends no `cursor`, later pages send the server's `nextCursor`, an absent or empty cursor ends the walk, and a cursor still present after 100 pages throws a plain Error naming the bound and the count. `createMcpConnector` closes the client when `listTools` throws, so the bound leaks no connection. On a declarative instance the provider classifies that throw as unavailable (degraded, retried with backoff) — see ③.
4. Public surface — unchanged: RIGHT. `MCP_TOOLS_LIST_MAX_PAGES` is exported from `mcp-connector.ts` for the tests and absent from `src/index.ts`; the package `exports` map carries `.` only, so no consumer reaches it. `McpClientLike.listTools` gains a documented obligation (every page) with no signature change. Nothing under `packages/spec` moves; `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError` and `isConnectorUpstreamUnavailable` are untouched.
5. The one live declarative `openapi` instance in the tree — unaffected: RIGHT. The showcase's `status-openapi.json` declares `openapi: "3.0.3"`, so the showcase boots as before; the Dogfood Regression Gate on this head agrees.

### ② Semver level

Two changesets — `@objectstack/connector-openapi: minor` and `@objectstack/connector-mcp: minor` — each carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, matching the PR body's two lines and the claim's. The level follows the kind: a non-`none` kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, and each diff moves only its own package. `narrowed` is right on connector-openapi: a value an author points `spec` at (a 2.0 document) is now refused. On connector-mcp nothing an author writes is newly refused; what narrows is the instance's accepted state at materialization (a server-rejected credential went from degraded to refused) — a requirement tightened, and the `semantic` reading lands on the same `minor`, so the level stands under either. Both carry the BREAKING banner, say what an upgrader sees and the remedy, and declare `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — honest: no spec key is added, removed or reshaped, `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and there is no tombstone to mint; the remedy is to the external document or to the credential, outside the metadata. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev-report deviations: (1) the shared checkout was moved to a detached HEAD inside the dev's own cloud container so the platform branch could be checked out in a worktree — no other seat shares that container, and all six commits on the branch are that session's; no effect on the reviewed tree. (2) The commits carry the model-free session and co-author trailer pair and no model identifier — verified on all six. (3) Ablations ran against `src/`, consistent with the tests' relative imports — nothing to answer.

open_questions[0] — a server still paging past the 100-page bound on a declarative instance; shipped A (degraded and retried): ANSWERED, A holds. The mcp provider already classifies every post-connect content fault as operational (a malformed `tools/list` answer lands in the same catch), the degraded reason surfaces the provider's message with the bound, and a retry costs at most 100 requests per attempt under the 5 s doubling to 5 min backoff. No config key can fix an over-paginating server, so a fatal classification would take a whole boot down for one upstream's behaviour.

open_questions[1] — ADR-0097's sentence "The `mcp` provider classifies connect / `tools/list` failures as unavailable": ESCALATED to the owning seat. A one-line amendment to that sentence (a 401/403 is a configuration fault) is owed under Prime Directive 13 and lives on a Tier H surface, so it lands by the maintainer's hand in its own PR, never in this one. Should-fix on the ADR, not a defect in this tree: the code applies the ADR's own configuration/operational split (an unresolvable `credentialRef` is fatal there, and so is the openapi provider's 401 on its spec fetch), the change is declared in the PR body, both changesets and the code comment, and the card that ordered it is maintainer-directed.

out_of_scope_findings: the programmatic `createOpenApiConnector` and the hand-wired `ConnectorOpenApiPlugin({ document })` path still trust their caller's document — as ADR-0023 states and as the card's item 2 names (`loadOpenApiDocument`). No action. Triage's p1 condition (a new `providerConfig` key returns to triage first) is honoured: items 1 and 3(c) are held back, the PR says `Refs`, not `Fixes`, and the card stays open with those items and item 4.

Noted for the seat, not a finding on this PR: a non-retryable 400/404/410 on the MCP endpoint still degrades and retries, asymmetric with the openapi spec fetch's treatment of the same statuses; the card asks for 401/403 only.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts — HOLDS. Tried to break it with: a numeric `openapi: 3` (refused, reported as declaring `3` — the specification requires a string); a `3.0.0-rc` suffix (refused; not a published shape); a document carrying both `swagger` and a 3.x `openapi` (loads as 3.x, the governing field); an inline document, which did no boot I/O before and does none now. The refusal names the source, what was found and the offline conversion, and carries no tracker number. The version check runs after every existing fault branch, so the retry/fatal split for URL specs is exactly what ADR-0097 records.

packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.test.ts — HOLDS. Each form (file, URL, inline) is pinned as a plain Error with `isConnectorUpstreamUnavailable` false and the source and remedy in the message; a missing field and 4.0.0 are pinned; 3.0.3, 3.1.0 and 3.1 are the positive control. No read escapes the package.

packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts — HOLDS. Tried: a server repeating the same cursor (bounded, throws, the client is closed); an empty-string `nextCursor` (read as the last page — the safer side, since re-sending an empty cursor is what a strict server would refuse); the first request carrying no `params.cursor` (pinned). Duplicate tool names across pages collapse onto one handler exactly as they already did within one page — pre-existing, not widened here.

packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts — HOLDS, one should-fix. The classification keys on the SDK's class and status, never on a numeric code of a JSON-RPC error, and the lazy import is of a hard dependency, so this failure path cannot be replaced by an import failure. Boot: plain throw, then `fail()`, fatal under both kernels; reload: logged and skipped with the previous live connector kept — the ADR-0097 reconcile policy. The appended SDK message carries the server's response body, never the request headers, so no credential is echoed. Should-fix (not blocking): `instanceof` binds the match to the SDK copy this package resolves, so an injected `clientFactory` built on a second SDK copy (a host pinning another `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) would miss the match and fall back to the previous degraded-and-retried classification, logged per attempt. A name-and-code check (`name === 'StreamableHTTPError'` with code 401/403, `name === 'UnauthorizedError'`) is as discriminating against `McpError` and copy-independent. Carrier: the seat, as a follow-up noted on the card.

packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.test.ts — HOLDS. Injected clients throw the SDK's real classes; 401 on `tools/list` pins the client close; a 403 nested in `cause` pins the walk; `StreamableHTTPError(503)` and `McpError(401)` are the controls that keep the old classification.

packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-http-discovery-faults.test.ts — HOLDS. A real localhost Streamable-HTTP fixture reached through the real SDK client: two pages pinned with the cursors the server actually received; the endless pager pinned at exactly 100 `tools/list` calls; 401 and 403 pinned as plain with exactly one request seen (no session DELETE, no SSE GET followed — the fixture answers GET with 405, the SDK's no-stream path); the declarative boot through `AutomationServicePlugin` + `ConnectorMcpPlugin` pinned to reject with no degraded reason and no second request after 300 ms. Servers close in `afterEach`, the kernel in `finally`; `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/core` were already devDependencies used by the existing plugin test. No read escapes the package.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-26709-connector-load-faults`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYmQXM3rHJcPnrEPk4B`

**VERDICT: PASS**
